title: Mock 2 · Products & Documents
blurb: Scheme structures, new-cadre products and the SID/SAI/KIM disclosure family, with a sweep of the other chapters.

questions.q: In the context of evaluating investments, 'liquidity' refers to:
options: The interest rate earned on the investment
How easily the investment can be converted to cash at fair value
The minimum amount needed to invest
The tax deduction available on the investment
questions.explanation: Liquidity is how easily an investment can be liquidated and converted to cash at fair value. Divisibility (partial sale) is also part of liquidity.
hints: That is the tax deduction factor.

questions.q: According to the workbook, which hidden costs are often missed when people compare doing their own investing with paying mutual fund fees?
options: The value of one's time and potential mistakes driven by emotional attachment
questions.explanation: People compare MF fees with a 'zero cost' DIY approach and miss the hidden costs: the time spent on research and administration, and emotion-driven mistakes.
hints: These are transaction levies, not the hidden DIY costs the workbook describes.
Partly relevant but not the workbook's point.

questions.q: The NAV of a mutual fund scheme also represents:
options: The net realisable value per unit if the scheme were liquidated
The face value of each unit
The total money raised in the NFO
The maximum price at which units can be sold
questions.explanation: NAV is the true worth of a unit and also the net realisable value per unit, i.e. how much money each unit would get if all holdings were sold and converted into cash.
hints: Face value is ₹10; NAV changes daily.
That relates to AUM at launch.
NAV is not a price ceiling.

questions.q: In an interval scheme, what are the minimum durations of the transaction period and the interval period?
questions.explanation: The transaction period (when the scheme opens for purchase and redemption) must be at least 2 days, and the interval period between transaction periods at least 15 days.

questions.q: What distinguishes an ETF from a regular open-ended index fund?
options: An ETF can be bought only during its NFO
An ETF trades on a stock exchange throughout the day at multiple prices
An ETF is always actively managed
questions.explanation: ETFs are traded on exchanges like shares, offering multiple intraday prices, whereas an open-ended fund transacts at a single end-of-day NAV.
hints: ETFs do have a NAV; the market price may differ from it.

questions.q: Which person is NOT eligible to be appointed a trustee of a mutual fund?
options: A person meeting the fit-and-proper criteria
A retired judge with no link to the AMC
A chartered accountant who furnishes all information sought by SEBI
A director of an asset management company
questions.explanation: Regulation 11 bars a director (including independent director), officer or employee of an AMC, and a trustee of any other mutual fund, from being a trustee.
hints: Fit-and-proper is a requirement, not a bar.

questions.q: Which statement about Registrars and Transfer Agents (RTAs) is correct?
options: RTAs are appointed by the trustees and need no registration
The AMC appoints the RTA, may keep the work in-house, and any RTA must be registered with SEBI
Appointing an external RTA is compulsory
questions.explanation: The AMC appoints the RTA. Appointing one is not compulsory (the work can be done in-house), but all RTAs must register with SEBI.
hints: Wrong appointer, and RTAs do need SEBI registration.

questions.q: Which of the following persons can be considered for empanelment as a new-cadre mutual fund distributor?
options: A retired bank officer with at least 10 years of service
A retired bank officer with 4 years of service
questions.explanation: The new cadre includes postal agents, retired government/semi-government officials (Class III and above) and retired bank officers with at least 10 years of service, and others such as bank correspondents notified by AMFI/AMCs.
hints: Not in the eligible list (and ARN needs age 18).
Needs at least 10 years of service.

questions.q: A liquid fund can invest only in debt and money market securities with a maturity of up to:
questions.explanation: Liquid funds invest only in debt and money market securities maturing within 91 days. Money market funds can go up to 1 year; overnight funds 1 day.
hints: That is the money market fund.

questions.q: Information about the sponsor, AMC, trustee company and service providers of a mutual fund is found in the:
questions.explanation: The SAI contains statutory information about the mutual fund and its constituents (sponsor, AMC, trustee company, custodian, RTA, auditor, etc.). One SAI applies to all schemes of the fund.

questions.q: For which schemes is NAV declared even on Sundays and holidays?
questions.explanation: Liquid and overnight funds declare NAV on Sundays and holidays too, reflecting that day's accrual. Close-ended schemes compute NAV at least weekly.

questions.q: By when must an AMC disclose the month-end portfolio of its equity schemes on its website and AMFI's website?
options: Within 10 days of the close of each month
questions.explanation: Portfolios (with ISIN) as of the last day of the month must be disclosed within 10 days. Debt schemes disclose fortnightly within 5 days.
hints: That is the debt-scheme fortnightly rule.

questions.q: On registering with MF Utilities, an investor receives a:
questions.explanation: MFU allots a Common Account Number (CAN) under which the investor's mutual fund holdings across participating AMCs are consolidated.
hints: PAN is issued by the Income Tax Department.

questions.q: An employee of a bank that distributes mutual funds must have NISM certification and also obtain:
options: A separate ARN in his own name
SEBI registration as an investment adviser
questions.explanation: Employees of institutional distributors obtain an Employee Unique Identification Number (EUIN) and work under the institution's ARN; no separate ARN is needed.
hints: They work under the institution's ARN.

questions.q: Which risk-adjusted measure uses Beta as the measure of risk?
questions.explanation: Treynor ratio = (Rs − Rf) ÷ Beta. It is most relevant for diversified equity schemes.
hints: IR uses the SD of excess returns.

questions.q: A scheme earned 4% in 6 months. Its simple annualised return is:
questions.explanation: Annualised = 4% × 12 ÷ 6 = 8% p.a.

questions.q: When market interest rates rise, the prices of existing bonds held by a debt fund generally:
questions.explanation: Interest rate risk: bond prices move inversely to interest rates.

questions.q: Units of an equity-oriented fund become a long-term capital asset if held for more than:
questions.explanation: There are only two holding periods: 12 months for listed securities and equity-oriented units, and 24 months for all other assets.

questions.q: What stamp duty applies when mutual fund units are issued against a purchase (lump sum, SIP, STP or switch-in)?
questions.explanation: From 1 July 2020, stamp duty of 0.005% applies on issue of units; transfers attract 0.015%.

questions.q: What happens to the value of an investor's holding when a scheme issues bonus units?
options: It remains the same; the number of units rises and the NAV falls proportionately
It rises by the bonus ratio
The investor must pay NAV for the bonus units
questions.explanation: Net assets stay the same; only the number of units increases, so NAV falls proportionately and the value of the holding is unchanged.
hints: More units offset the lower NAV.

questions.q: Under ASBA, when does the application money actually leave the investor's bank account?
questions.explanation: In ASBA the bank blocks the amount; it is debited only on allotment, so it keeps earning interest and no refund is needed.
hints: Not linked to the opening date.

questions.q: A Power of Attorney holder operating a folio can carry out all transactions EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: A PoA holder can conduct all transactions except making or changing nominations.

questions.q: Which statement about an investment made in the name of a minor is correct?
options: The minor can have up to two joint holders
KYC of the minor alone is sufficient
The investment is made through a guardian and cannot have joint holders
questions.explanation: A minor invests through a guardian (natural parent or court-appointed), who completes KYC; a minor's investment cannot have joint holders.
hints: Minors can't contract; the guardian acts.

questions.q: SEBI permits celebrity endorsements of mutual funds:
options: For any scheme, if the AMC pays
Only at industry level for awareness of MFs as a product category, with SEBI's prior approval
questions.explanation: Celebrity endorsements are allowed only at industry level to raise awareness, cannot promote a particular scheme or AMC brand, are funded from pooled investor-education money and need SEBI's prior approval.
hints: Not limited to NFOs; scheme promotion is barred.

questions.q: If unitholders feel the trustees have breached their obligations, whom can they file a suit against?
questions.explanation: A trust is a notional entity, so investors cannot sue the trust; they can sue the trustees for breach of trust.
hints: A trust can't be sued; it is notional.
